key_insight: By extending online-to-nonconvex conversion to composite objectives, the paper shows that adding a convex regularizer does not worsen oracle complexity for stochastic nonsmooth nonconvex optimization.
engineering_relevance: This gives a principled way to train constrained or regularized models with provably optimal query complexity, including settings relevant to large-scale machine learning and inverse problems.
method: Use online-to-nonconvex conversion with an online learner to choose update directions.
Redefine the learner’s losses to include the convex regularizer directly, rather than linearizing it.
Apply a variant of online mirror descent to obtain low regret and Goldstein-type stationarity guarantees.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical oracle complexity bounds of O(δ^-1 ε^-3) stochastic gradient queries or O(d δ^-1 ε^-3) function-value queries, matching known optimal rates for noncomposite problems, plus numerical experiments.
watch_item: The guarantees are complexity-theoretic and depend on Goldstein stationarity parameters, so practical performance may be sensitive to the choice of δ, ε, and the quality of stochastic oracle estimates.
paper_title: Composite Online-to-Nonconvex Conversion with Optimal Oracle Complexity
